rationale: Round 1 compiled, ran correctly, and hit no ICE fallback, so this round escalates obfuscation strength while respecting the profile's hot numeric core. planetpv (3500 of 4417 text bytes) is a dense floating-point loop, so control-flow passes get the highest security weights: FLA (0.90) and BCF (0.75) to break the loop-structure an analyst would target first, with SUB at 0.85 since arithmetic-expression substitution is cheap and especially effective on the constant-heavy numeric code in almabench/fftbench/lpbench. IBR (0.80) and ICALL (0.75) add indirection to obscure branch and call targets, and IGV (0.70) plus a strong DiversityGain (0.75) diversifies global access patterns at low runtime cost. SPLIT stays moderate — it is nearly free and amplifies FLA/BCF by enlarging the region they scramble. Runtime and size costs are kept moderately weighted (BCF/FLA highest at 0.55-0.60) so the selector still hesitates to stack the expensive passes inside the hottest inner loops, and correctness risk stays ≤0.25 everywhere given the correctness-sensitive reference outputs of these benchmark kernels.
